The pairing of the two helices of DNA is such that $A$ pairs with $T$ and $G$ pairs with $C$, through hydrogen bonding.

number of $\mathrm{G}=$ number of $\mathrm{C}$
Therefore, statement in Assertion (A) is wrong and Reason (R) is correct.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which of the following vitamins cannot be stored in the body?
questions.solution:
Vitamins are classified into two groups depending upon their solubility in water or fat.

Fat soluble vitamins: Vitamins which are soluble in fat and oils but insoluble in water are kept in this group. These are vitamins A, D, E and K. They are stored in liver and adipose (fat storing) tissues.

Water soluble vitamins: B group vitamins and vitamin C are soluble in water. Water soluble vitamins must be supplied regularly in diet because they are readily excreted in urine and cannot be stored (except vitamin B12) in our body.

questions.solution: Chemically, peptide linkage is an amide formed abetween –COOH group and –NH2 group. The reaction between two molecules of similar or different amino acids, proceeds through the combination of the amino group of one molecule with the carboxyl group of the other. This results in the elimination of a water molecule and formation of a peptide bond –CO–NH–. The product of the reaction is called a dipeptide because it is made up of two amino acids. For example, when carboxyl group of glycine combines with the amino group of alanine we get a dipeptide, glycylalanine

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
Which of the following statements are true about carbohydrates?
(i) Monosaccharides can be hydrolysed.
(ii) The two monosaccharide units obtained on hydrolysis of a disaccharide can either be same or different.
(iii) Polysaccharides are now sweet in taste.
(iv) All monosaccharides are not reducing. sugars.
questions.solution:
(i) Monosaccharides are smallest carbohydrates that cannot be hydrolysed.
So, statement (i) is not true.
(ii) Disaccharides are made up of two units of monosaccharides, so their hydrolysis will also give two monosaccharide unit that can be same or different.
e.g., Sucrose $\longrightarrow$ Glucose + Fructose
Maltose $\longrightarrow$ Glucose + Glucose
So, statement (ii) is true.
(iii) Polysaccharides are polymers of many monosaccharides and have no sweet taste.
So, statements (iii) is true.
(iv) Monosaccharides are categorised as reducing and non-reducing sugars.
So, statement (iv) is not true.

questions.q:
Assertion (A): An optically active amino acid can exit in three forms depending on the pH of the solution.

Reason (R): Amino acids contain both acidic and basic groups, they exist as zwetter ion in aq. medium, anionic form in acidic medium and cationic form in basic medium
options: <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi mathvariant="normal">A</mi></math> and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi mathvariant="normal">R</mi></math> are correct and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi mathvariant="normal">R</mi></math> is the correct explanation for <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi mathvariant="normal">A</mi></math>

<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi mathvariant="normal">A</mi></math> and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi mathvariant="normal">R</mi></math> are correct but <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi mathvariant="normal">R</mi></math> is not the correct explanation for <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi mathvariant="normal">A</mi></math>
<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi mathvariant="normal">A</mi></math> is correct, <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi mathvariant="normal">R</mi></math> is wrong
<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi mathvariant="normal">A</mi></math> is wrong, <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi mathvariant="normal">R</mi></math> is correct
questions.solution:
We know that amino acids can exist as a zwitter ion form which contains both positive and negative charge and in cationic form it exist in acidic medium because acid furnish H+ which is abstracted by a base (-NH2), while in alkaline medium base is there which is capable of abstracting a proton from the carboxylic acid and so it also exists as anionic form.

Hence, we can conclude that depending on the pH of the solution an optically active amino acid can exit in three forms.

Therefore, Assertion is correct but reason is wrong.

questions.solution: Watson and Crick proposed that DNA molecule is in the form of a double helix with two polynucleotide chains coiled around one another in a spiral. This is known as B-DNA or biological DNA. It has 10 nucleotides pairs per turn of the double helix and is right handed with a diameter of \(20 Å\). One complete turn of the double helix is \(34 Å\). The distance between adjacent stacks or nucleotides is \(3.4 Å\). Hence, option (d) is correct.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
Which of the following statements are correct?
(A) A tripeptide had two peptide bonds.
(B) A pentapeptide contains five amino acids.
(C) Nucleotide is a product of base and sugar.
(D) In cellulose, \(\boldsymbol{\beta}\)-glycosidic linkages are present.
questions.solution:
The explanations of given statements are as follows:
(A) A tripetide contains 3 amino acids linked by two peptide linkages. Thus, statement (A) is correct.
(B) A pentapeptide contains five amino acids linked by four peptide linkages. Thus, statement (B) is also correct.
(C) Nucleoside is a product of base and sugar. Thus, statements (C) is incorrect.
(D) In cellulose, \(\beta\)-D-glucose units are joined by glycosidic linkage between \(\mathrm{C}-\mathrm{l}\) of, one glucose and C-4 of the next glucose unit. Thus, statement (D) is a also correct.
Hence, option (c) is correct.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which one of the following enzymes converts proteins into amino acids?
questions.solution: The enzymatic activity of trypsin converts proteins into amino acids. Trypsin is a pancreatic enzyme, which activates the other pancreatic enzymes like chymotrypsin, carboxy polypeptidase, etc. These enzymes along with trypsin convert proteins and peptones into dipeptides first and then finally into amino acids.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
Observe the following statements.
I. Sucrose has glycosidic linkage.
II. Cellulose is present in both plants and animals.
III. Lactose contains D-galactose and D-glucose units.
Which of the following statements are correct?
questions.solution:
Let's evaluate each statement to determine which are correct.
- Statement I: Sucrose has a glycosidic linkage. This is correct. Sucrose is a disaccharide formed by a glycosidic linkage between a glucose unit and a fructose unit.
- Statement II: Cellulose is present in both plants and animals. This is incorrect. Cellulose is the main structural component of the primary cell wall of green plants, but it's not present in animals. Animals lack the enzyme cellulase to break down cellulose.
- Statement III: Lactose contains D-galactose and D-glucose units. This is correct. Lactose is a disaccharide commonly known as milk sugar. It's composed of one molecule of Dgalactose and one molecule of D-glucose, joined by a \(\beta\)-1,4-glycosidic linkage.
Therefore, the correct statements are I and III. The correct option is (4).

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: How many tripeptides can be prepared by linking the amino acids glycine, alanine and phenyl alanine?
questions.solution:
Tripeptides are amino acids polymers in which three individual amino acid units, called residues, are linked together by amide bonds. In these, an amine group from one residue forms an amide bond with the carboxyl group of a second residue, the amino group of the second forms an amide bond with the carboxyl group of the third. Therefore, glycine $\left(\mathrm{NH}_2-\mathrm{CH}_2-\mathrm{COOH}\right)$,alanine
and phenyl alanine
can be linked in six different ways.
